law: delayMs <= 0 is an unthrottled continuation that runs before any pending deadline and advances the clock by nothing; delayMs > 0 is a deadline honoured to the millisecond; every request is cancellable; requests sharing a key coalesce to one run at the earliest deadline with the newest callback; ties run in enqueue order.
provenance: ticket 2026/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END — 📓️audit-extension-hop-latency-2026-09-12.md measured two silent ~11-13 s gaps per extension hop in a headless page, caused by the guest's Effect::DispatchAction{delay_ms:0} re-arm riding a nested setTimeout chain that Chrome clamps to ~1 tick/s when the renderer is hidden or unfocused. Natively the same chain is 0.58 s.

cases.name: zero-delay-outruns-a-pending-deadline
cases.law: A continuation never queues behind a deadline that has not arrived, however early that deadline was armed.

cases.name: a-deadline-is-honoured-to-the-millisecond
cases.law: delayMs > 0 still means what it says: deadlines run in deadline order, not enqueue order.

cases.name: continuations-preserve-enqueue-order
cases.law: Zero-delay work is a FIFO, not a set: the host's effect order survives the hop across the event loop.

cases.name: a-cancelled-deadline-never-runs
cases.law: Cancellation before the deadline drops the callback and leaves every other request untouched.

cases.name: a-cancelled-continuation-never-runs
cases.law: Cancellation works on the unthrottled lane too, right up to the macrotask that drains it.

cases.name: a-ten-hop-rearm-chain-costs-no-wall-clock
cases.law: THE regression law: the guest's Effect::DispatchAction{delay_ms:0} re-arm, chained ten deep, finishes at millisecond zero. On a nested setTimeout chain in a hidden renderer the same ten hops cost ten seconds.

cases.name: a-key-coalesces-to-the-earliest-deadline
cases.law: Two wakes for one owner are one wake: the later request replaces the callback and the earlier deadline wins, so coalescing can only ever make work sooner.

cases.name: a-key-keeps-the-newest-callback
cases.law: The mirror of the case above: asking again for LATER does not push the run out, and the newest callback is the one that runs.
